citation: Bedford L, Hay D, Devoy A, Paine S, Powe DG, Seth R, Gray T, Topham I, Fone K, Rezvani N, Mee M, Soane T, Layfield R, Sheppard PW, Ebendal T, Usoskin D, Lowe J, Mayer RJ. Depletion of 26S proteasomes in mouse brain neurons causes neurodegeneration and Lewy-like inclusions resembling human pale bodies. The Journal of Neuroscience. 2008;28(33):8189-8198. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2218-08.2008.
description: This target-specific mouse study conditionally deleted Psmc1/Rpt2 in neurons and showed selective 26S proteasome depletion, ubiquitin-positive inclusions, and extensive neurodegeneration in targeted forebrain or nigrostriatal neurons. It supports the expectation that Psmc1 loss impairs neuronal proteasome function and pushes neurons toward proteotoxic injury rather than a silent state.

citation: Radhakrishnan SK, den Besten W, Deshaies RJ. p97-dependent retrotranslocation and proteolytic processing govern formation of active Nrf1 upon proteasome inhibition. eLife. 2014;3:e01856. doi:10.7554/eLife.01856.
description: This paper showed that compromised proteasomes stabilize and process Nrf1/NFE2L1, enabling activation of proteasome subunit gene expression as a compensatory bounce-back response. It provides the directional prior that proteasome insufficiency should increase proteasome subunit mRNAs such as Psmc3, Psmc4, Psmc6, Psmd1, Psmd3, Psmd9, and Psme4.

citation: Oron M, Grochowski M, Jaiswar A, Legierska J, Jastrzebski K, Nowak-Niezgoda M, Kolos M, Kazmierczak W, Olesinski T, Lenarcik M, Cybulska M, Mikula M, Zylicz A, Miaczynska M, Zettl K, Wisniewski JR, Walerych D. The molecular network of the proteasome machinery inhibition response is orchestrated by HSP70, revealing vulnerabilities in cancer cells. Cell Reports. 2022;40:111428. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111428.
description: Global profiling after proteasome inhibition identified molecular chaperones, the unfolded-protein response, autophagy, and endocytosis-related proteins as major compensatory programs, with HSPA1A/B central to the response. This supports the observed induction of Hsp70/Hsp90/Dnajb genes and other proteostasis markers after Psmc1 perturbation.

citation: Qiao S, Lamore SD, Cabello CM, Lesson JL, Munoz-Rodriguez JL, Wondrak GT. Thiostrepton is an inducer of oxidative and proteotoxic stress that impairs viability of human melanoma cells but not primary melanocytes. Biochemical Pharmacology. 2012;83:1229-1247. doi:10.1016/j.bcp.2012.01.027.
description: Thiostrepton-driven proteotoxic stress impaired proteasomal activity, accumulated ubiquitinated proteins, induced heat-shock genes including HSPA1A, DNAJB4, HSPH1, and HSPA5, increased the ER-stress gene DDIT3, and modulated pro-apoptotic BAX. It links loss of proteasome function to the specific heat-shock, ER-stress, and apoptotic transcript classes seen in the large Psmc1 responses.
